scorecard.note: The hook, beats and closing all say the same thing (bleaching every 2 years, with no time to recover). Open on a concrete, human-scale threat, such as 'The Great Barrier Reef is dying faster than it can heal', and use the beats to build tow

storyboard.ears: Reef bleaching now returns about every 2 years.
The reef has already suffered 3 bleaching events this decade. What was rare became routine.
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) | Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching events per decade | https://aims.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-04/FINAL-Aerial%20Bleaching%20GBR2024Report_AIMS_Final_15Apr2024_0.pdf | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: The average gap shrank to 2 years. The reef barely catches its breath.
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) | Years between Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching events | https://aims.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-04/FINAL-Aerial%20Bleaching%20GBR2024Report_AIMS_Final_15Apr2024_0.pdf | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: A reef typically needs 10 years to recover. New bleaching arrives far too soon.
storyboard.evidence: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) / NOAA Coral Reef Watch | Coral recovery time vs time actually between bleaching events | https://aims.gov.au | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Each bleaching wave now arrives before the reef can fully recover.
